stem:
Bhavna must locate every point that is $6\,\mathrm{cm}$ from point $P$ and also $6\,\mathrm{cm}$ from point $Q$.

Which two claims correctly locate those points?

options.text: Take the intersection points of the circle centred at $P$ with radius $6\,\mathrm{cm}$ and the circle centred at $Q$ with radius $6\,\mathrm{cm}$.
Take the intersection points of an arc of radius $6\,\mathrm{cm}$ drawn from $P$ with an arc of radius $6\,\mathrm{cm}$ drawn from $Q$.
Treat point $P$ itself as every such point.
Take the midpoint of segment $PQ$ only because $6$ is printed, without drawing equal-radius arcs.

teacher.key_rationale: Points at distance 6 cm from both P and Q are the intersections of equal-radius 6 cm circles or arcs from P and Q. Naming P alone, or grabbing the midpoint from the printed 6 without arcs, miss that locus.
